item.title: CI/CD and Code Review
item.description:
Now, review runs continuously, more like spellcheck while you write. Most changes have been reviewed and fixed by Claude at least once before a human is asked to look. This catches most routine mistakes, and saves team attention for higher-level questions and scrutiny.

  • Anthropic’s recent post on code review

As we move through big shifts in software dev practices, it’s grounding to get historical context and realize that much of what we do is more recent than we thought. In the 90s/00s, it wasn’t that uncommon for small teams to just push to trunk directly (as long as the build/test times were fast):

item.title: An Opinionated Guide to Python Projects
item.description:
Updated on: 2026-10-18.

This post is meant to be an opinionated guide to setting up and developing a Python project. The goal is to give a paved path that avoids common snags.

Let uv manage Python

Python project management has become drastically simpler with the introduction of uv (which consolidated many tools and made everything way faster). There are a few main things it will handle for you: setting up a project structure, installing Python, and installing the dependencies.

item.title: Unicode, String Encodings, and Python
item.description:
I’ve been working on the cryptopals challenges and avoiding stock libraries, to learn more about string encodings and the bytes type in Python 3. So here, we’ll learn way more than we need to know about Unicode.

Text as Unicode Strings

To work with text data, computers need to work with many different types of characters. From all the world’s languages to symbols to emojis, the list goes on. Unicode1 is a specification that aims to give every character used in human texts its own unique and standard code.
